To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
microtubules regulate spine morphology and synaptic plasticity via regulation of p140Cap/Snip localization to spines and cortactin activity.
microtubule end tracking proteins, EB1 and EB3, are present in spines and that their inhibition or knockdown results in spine morphological changes.
dynamic microtubule tips enter spines, regulate spine morphology via p140Cap and cortactin, and are required for long-term potentiation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of microtubules in regulating the morphology and function of dendritic spines.
the molecular mechanisms that control dendritic spine morphology and synaptic plasticity, and how microtubule growth and actin dynamics are regulated by microtubule-associated proteins.
the role of the microtubules in the regulation of the actine cytoskeleton in dendritic spines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
microtubules regulate spine morphology and function via the EB3-p140Cap-Src-cortactin signaling pathway.

dynamic microtubule tips regulate the localization of the EB3-binding protein p140Cap within spines, and p140Cap controls the function of cortactin, a F-actin regulator that modulates actin dynamics within spines.
dynamic microtubule tips regulate spine shape and synaptic plasticity by modulating actin dynamics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EB3-labled microtubule tips regulate p140Cap and cortactin function and modulate spine morphology and synaptic plasticity.
dynamic microtubule regulation of actin dynamics is a key component of spine morphological plasticity.
the dynamic microtubule cytoskeleton is an important component of dendritic spines that regulates spine morphologies via the regulation of Src signaling and the actin cytokeleton.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the growing ends of microtubules are able to regulate the actin cyto-skeleton in dendritic spines and thus modulate spine morphology and synaptic plasticity.
microtubule tips are involved in regulating spine shape and function.
dynamic microtubule tips regulate spine shape via the actin cytokeleton.
